concepts.heading: Jealousy as Information
concepts.alt: A guide reading a letter from an envelope sealed with a small green flame
concepts.plain: Jealousy is a message worth reading. It is not proof of love and not a flaw.

concepts.heading: The Anatomy of Jealousy
concepts.alt: A guide holding a set of nesting dolls, each with a different feeling face
concepts.plain: Jealousy is usually several feelings mixed, like fear, sadness and feeling left out.

concepts.heading: Why Suppression Doesn't Work
concepts.alt: A guide pushing a beach ball under water as it pops back up
concepts.plain: Pushing jealousy down does not work. It comes back stronger.

concepts.heading: Why Impulsive Action Doesn't Work Either
concepts.alt: About to press a big red button and stopping his own hand
concepts.plain: Acting on it right away, with demands or snooping, also backfires.

concepts.heading: The Middle Path
concepts.alt: A guide walking along a balanced middle path between two ditches
concepts.plain: The middle way: feel it, work out what it is about, then ask for what you need.

concepts.heading: Normalizing Jealousy
concepts.alt: All raising a hand with a knowing smile
concepts.plain: Everyone feels jealous sometimes, even people with years of practice.

checks.after: Why Impulsive Action Doesn't Work Either
checks.prompt: Which is an example of acting on jealousy impulsively?
options: Demanding a partner end another relationship
checks.explanation: Demanding a partner end another relationship. Impulsive reactions include demanding a partner end another relationship, issuing ultimatums and snooping.

checks.prompt: Do secure, experienced people still feel jealousy?
options: Yes, even the most experienced do
checks.explanation: Yes, even the most experienced do. Everyone feels jealousy, including happily married people and people with decades of non-monogamous experience.

89bb3c92-9cc6-4a90-b9ff-db7001d55f1c.takeaway: Jealousy is a signal. Notice it, find what is underneath, then say what you need.

concepts.heading: The HEARTS Framework: Building Security
concepts.alt: A guide holding a large glowing heart-shaped shield
concepts.plain: HEARTS is six habits that help partners feel safe with each other.

concepts.heading: H — Here (Being Present and Attuned)
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting together, A putting her phone face down to give B her full attention
concepts.plain: Here: when you are with someone, really be with them.

concepts.heading: E — Expressed Delight
concepts.alt: C lighting up with joy and opening her arms as D arrives
concepts.plain: Expressed delight: show your partner you are glad they exist.

concepts.heading: A — Attunement
concepts.alt: A noticing B's worried face and leaning in gently
concepts.plain: Attunement: notice how they feel, even before they say it.

concepts.heading: R — Rituals and Routines
concepts.alt: Two guides clinking mugs at a table under a wall calendar with a heart on every week
concepts.plain: Rituals: small things you do regularly that they can count on.

concepts.heading: T — Turning Toward
concepts.alt: A guide turning around with a smile toward a small waving hand
concepts.plain: Turning toward: answer their small reaches for connection.

concepts.heading: S — Security
concepts.alt: A guide standing beside a small glowing lighthouse
concepts.plain: Security: be the safe home base they can return to.

concepts.heading: HEARTS in Your Own Relationships
concepts.plain: Use HEARTS in whatever relationships you have, and plan your energy for it.

checks.prompt: What does the A in HEARTS stand for?
checks.explanation: Attunement. Tuning into your partner's emotional states, even when they haven't explicitly communicated them.

options: A reliable, safe base your partner can explore from
checks.explanation: A reliable, safe base your partner can explore from. Creating a reliable, safe base from which your partner can explore — including their other relationships.

66cd2ad9-8704-41d6-8b79-e74540455f1f.takeaway: HEARTS: be here, show delight, tune in, keep rituals, turn toward, and be a safe base.

mnemonic.caption: Six habits that help a partner feel safe with you

concepts.heading: Attachment Patterns in Relationships
concepts.alt: A guide holding a childhood photo frame tied by a ribbon to her heart
concepts.plain: How you learned to feel safe as a child shows up in adult relationships.

concepts.heading: Anxious Attachment
concepts.alt: Anxiously checking his phone
concepts.plain: Anxious pattern: lots of worry, checking and needing reassurance.

concepts.heading: Avoidant Attachment
concepts.alt: A guide stepping back with a hand up, keeping a wide space around her
concepts.plain: Avoidant pattern: keeping distance and pulling away when things get close.

concepts.heading: Disorganized Attachment
concepts.alt: A guide stepping forward with one foot and backward with the other, torn
concepts.plain: Disorganized pattern: wanting closeness and fearing it, often after early hurt.

concepts.heading: How Relationships Can Trigger — or Heal — Attachment Wounds
concepts.plain: Relationships can stir up these patterns, and steady ones help heal them.

concepts.heading: The Path to Earned Security
concepts.alt: Two guides planting a small tree together
concepts.plain: You can earn security: know your pattern, say what you need, choose steady people.

checks.prompt: Which pattern tends to check for replies, read silence as rejection and need frequent reassurance?
checks.explanation: Anxious attachment. Anxious attachment looks like checking your phone for replies, reading silence as rejection and needing frequent reassurance.
Recognizing your patterns without shame. Earned security isn't about eliminating anxiety or avoidance. It starts with recognizing your patterns without shame.

0f63e2fa-4582-4082-9fe6-0e1729fd974e.takeaway: Old patterns of clinging or pulling away can be understood and changed with practice.

concepts.heading: Cultivating Compersion
concepts.alt: A guide smiling warmly while watching two small hearts float upward
concepts.plain: Compersion is feeling happy that your partner is happy with someone else.

concepts.heading: What Compersion Is — and Isn't
concepts.alt: Calmly holding a happy heart in one hand and a small green flame in the other
concepts.plain: It is a real feeling you cannot force, and it can sit alongside jealousy.

concepts.heading: The Path to Compersion
concepts.alt: A guide watering a flower bed where a heart-shaped flower is opening
concepts.plain: It tends to show up when you feel safe, included and cared for.

concepts.heading: When Compersion Doesn't Come
concepts.alt: A guide shrugging gently with a kind smile
concepts.plain: Sometimes it never comes. That is okay. You are not doing it wrong.

concepts.heading: Managing NRE (New Relationship Energy)
concepts.alt: A floating upward holding heart balloons while B kindly holds her hand to keep her grounded
concepts.plain: New love is exciting. Keep showing up for the people you already have.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Professional Support
concepts.plain: If jealousy is hurting your life, a therapist who respects your relationship style can help.

options: Feeling joy at your partner's joy
checks.explanation: Feeling joy at your partner's joy. Compersion — sometimes called "the opposite of jealousy" — is the experience of feeling joy at your partner's joy, even when it has nothing to do with you.
That's completely okay. And sometimes it just doesn't — and that's completely okay. Not feeling compersion doesn't mean you're doing anything wrong.

ee7c8f7f-bbaf-46be-96d3-4ee04adec296.takeaway: Feeling glad for your partner's joy can grow with time, and it is fine if it does not.
